## Highlights since 0.19.2

- **Typst documents.** The native Lattice now opens, highlights and builds Typst (`.typ`) documents, with a live preview as you type and errors you can click. The Typst compiler is a one-time download of about 22 MB, which Lattice offers the first time you build a Typst document; Settings › Editor & builds › Typst support removes it or downloads it again.
- **Highlighting for code files.** In the native Lattice, Python, TypeScript and TSX, JavaScript and JSX, Rust, Go, C, C++, Java, R, Lua, shell scripts, YAML, TOML, JSON, Makefiles, Dockerfiles and CSS files open with syntax highlighting, and so do Markdown code blocks in these languages.
- **Set Markdown table row heights.** In the native Lattice's visual Markdown editor, drag a row's bottom border to make the row taller, or double-click the border to fit the row to its content again. Lattice remembers the heights with the column widths, and the `.md` file stays plain Markdown.

## Notable fixes

- On macOS 27.3, the Agent's message box no longer disappears when a draft reaches a second line, for example after Shift+Return (#1227).
- Live preview no longer spins on "First layout…" forever, in both versions of Lattice. After a minute without a layout, its pill says live preview is taking long and offers Reinstall live preview. Lattice now checks every file of the installed live preview engine, so it downloads it once more (about 4 MB) after this update.
- In the native Lattice, the pointer shows the right cursor again over parts of the window that pass their input through the app, such as the I-beam over text.
